about: Direction-labelled currency-exchange questions (backlog E3.1). Every item names a FROM currency (what the person has or pays with) and a TO currency (what they want), labelled BY HAND from the meaning of the sentence -- never from word order. The sweep-181 bench's truth was positional (first currency named = FROM) and wrong on 29 of 74 directional CLINC150 train items; these labels are the correction. Sentences with no direction are listed under 'skipped' with the reason, so every one of the 150 CLINC150 exchange_rate sentences is accounted for.

fields.from_words/to_words: the exact words that named each currency (the from_question verdict a model would give)
fields.from_at/to_at: token index of those words under the tokenizer in split_rule
fields.amount_in: which currency the amount counts (often the TO side: 'buy 200 euros with dollars')
fields.to_also: extra TO currencies when one amount is asked in several
fields.clinc_split: the CLINC150 split the sentence came from
fields.split: train | test, the deterministic split every consumer must use
fields.skipped[].words: for SYMMETRIC skipped sentences: the two currency words, in order -- the probe that a direction is REFUSED ('either' verdicts are taught from the train half)

split_rule: tokens = re.findall(r'\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?|[a-z]+|[$\u20ac\u00a3\u00a5]', text.lower()); h = int(sha256(('exchange_direction:' + ' '.join(tokens)).encode()).hexdigest()[:8], 16); split = 'test' if h % 100 < 35 else 'train'
attribution: Items with source 'clinc150' are sentences from CLINC150 (Larson et al., 'An Evaluation Dataset for Intent Classification and Out-of-Scope Prediction', EMNLP 2019; https://github.com/clinc/oos-eval), licensed CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). The direction labels, word spans, amounts and the hand-written items are leCore's own (2026-09-26).
